displayOrder.name: Compact Catalogue
displayOrder.prompt:
Usecase: ui-mockup. Create ONE realistic production-quality macOS PokeTaskBar main-window mockup for Collection → Shop. Target 1488×1056 landscape. Render complete window straight-on with native traffic lights, full bottom corners, outer inset margins. No browser, presentation framing, option numbers, captions outside the app or multiple screenshots.
References 1 and 2 are the APPROVED Bag and Storage. Preserve their shared macOS shell, expanded left navigation and calm Linear-like inset rounded main canvas. References 3,4,5 are exact in-app Rare Candy, Shiny Charm and egg sprites: use their recognizable pixel appearance. Mint uses a small green leaf. Keep sprites proportional and crisp. No smooth 3D art.
Shell #EFF0F2, main canvas #F8F8FA, grouped surfaces #FFFFFF, ink #242528, metadata #73757B. SF Pro-like typography 14–16 body, 28–32 headings. Neutral selected backgrounds and restrained small blue accents. Main canvas inset on ALL four sides; sidebars blend into shell. ABSOLUTELY NO permanent sidebar separator strokes, full-height lines, edge-to-edge section rules, or resting resize grips/dots. Separation through whitespace, open gutters and subtle surface tone. No decorative gradients, glow, glass or card stacks.
Expanded left navigation approx240px: PokeTaskBar, Cody, Search, Today, Focus, Issues, Projects, Initiatives, Collection selected, Usage, Settings at bottom. Native top toolbar back/forward, Collection page tab and small sidebar collapse/reopen buttons. Right extras collapsed for these proposals: all essential data/actions stay in main canvas.
Main page heading Collection. Local navigation Bag / Storage / Pokédex / Shop with SHOP selected. Secondary title Shop. Quiet balance "12,500 Coins" labelled "Available". These are earned in-app Coins, never dollars or payment cards. Compact Open Bag and Open Storage text links stay in main header or footer, not sidebar-only.
EXACT six existing products at default shop difficulty, sorted low-to-high price with the ALREADY OWNED passive Shiny Charm LAST:
1 Mint — 1,000 Coins — "2× XP for 30 minutes" — "Owned 2" — Buy.
2 Rare Candy — 5,000 Coins — "+1.5M XP when used" — "Owned 5" — Buy.
3 Pokémon Egg — 10,000 Coins — "Adds an egg to Storage" — Buy.
4 Uncommon Egg — 25,000 Coins — "Uncommon or better" — subtle Uncommon badge — "Not enough Coins".
5 Rare Egg — 40,000 Coins — "Rare or better" — subtle Rare badge — "Not enough Coins".
6 Shiny Charm — ALREADY OWNED, passive, permanent, "Improves shiny hatch chance" — "Owned · Active" with quiet check mark. NO Buy, Use, quantity or repeat-purchase controls. Price not necessary once owned.
All three eggs use the SAME ivory-and-green egg sprite; distinguish tiers through labels/badges only. No legendary egg, recolored magical eggs, random invented products, categories, deals, bundles, cart, checkout, money purchases, countdowns or sales pressure.
Purchase flow: clicking Buy opens a small inline confirmation and final Buy / Cancel controls at that product; no modal sheet. Buying a Mint or Rare Candy adds one to Bag without applying it. Buying an egg sends it to Storage and leaves the current Lapras training; success opens Storage. Current raising Pokémon is Lapras, not an egg. The screenshot shows either idle state or the direction's specified inline confirmation.
Actual selected product remains affordable against 12,500 Coins. Never offer active Buy for 25,000 or40,000. No training/Use item on Shop. Compact useful copy and generous breathing room; simple honest purchase state. No search/sort/filter toolbar necessary for six products.

Product name16ptsemibold, effectdescription14pt, ownedcountsmall. Anchor price and Buy action to lower edge of each affordable card. Buttons quietneutral; blue onlyfocusaccent.

All six cards fully visible above maincanvasbottom; no cutoff, no three-rowlist disguisedascards. Undergrid a single calm helper line "Eggs go to Storage. Your current Pokémon keeps training." and compact OpenBag / OpenStorage links. Restofcanvas generousair. No rightsidebar. Beautiful precise compactmacOSappdesign, not storefrontmarketing.

implementationNotes: Shop remains Collection > Shop; reuse local Bag / Storage / Pokédex / Shop navigation.

Prices shown use existing base prices at default shop difficulty 1.0: Mint 1,000; Rare Candy 5,000; basic Pokémon Egg 10,000; Uncommon Egg 25,000; Shiny Charm 30,000; Rare Egg 40,000 Coins. Production prices come from store.price with current shopDifficulty, never fixed display literals.

Mock balance 12,500 Coins and inventory five Rare Candy, two Mint and an owned Shiny Charm are illustrative, consistent with the approved Bag reference. Shiny Charm is sorted last because it is already owned.
Preserve price ascending ordering with purchased passive items last. Available products remain the three existing item kinds and three existing egg tiers; no legendary egg.
Mint boosts XP 2x for 30 minutes; it does not change nature. Rare Candy grants 1.5M XP when used from Bag. Purchases add inventory and do not immediately apply an item.
Purchase controls confirm inline, with Buy and Cancel. Option 3 demonstrates this confirmation for a basic Pokémon Egg: 12,500 minus 10,000 leaves 2,500 Coins.

Selecting a product changes only the preview, not purchase state. Confirming must be cleared or rebound to the specific selected product; each purchase revalidates affordability and existing eligibility.
Buying an egg banks it in Storage and opens Storage; the current partner remains training. No new training or item-use actions belong on Shop.
Owned Shiny Charm shows Owned / Active, no repeat purchase, quantity or Use action. All three egg tiers share the existing egg sprite and use names/badges to distinguish guaranteed rarity floors.
Insufficient balance is a legible quiet state with no active purchase control; preserve eligibility even when the active partner is an egg.
Right extras may stay collapsed; balance, product details, confirmation and links remain in the main canvas. Independently collapsible/resizable sidebars use the approved hover-only boundary guide.
The no-separator rule remains authoritative: remove incidental generated local footer/card rules or vertical link dividers; no permanent major-section or sidebar separator strokes.
Keep sprite proportions and existing pixel assets. Responsive layout must preserve readable prices, statuses, keyboard focus and visible confirmation controls.
